messages:
maya: quick heads-up — after rolling back the kernel-hint patch yesterday we still see a 15-25% tail latency bump on mistral7b workloads (p95/p99).
alex: ugh, seen the graphs. Is this only on GQA or does MQA show it too?
maya: mostly GQA paths, but a smaller effect on MQA when num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads (we have a couple of model variants with mismatched kv heads).
jiro: can you paste the lightweight profile? maybe kernel selection is picking slow matmul path because of odd headstride.
maya: pasted below — main suspect is kernel fallback for headstride 96 -> fallback to slower generic kernel. also paged KV layout shows fragmentation spikes.
```
PROFILE SUMMARY (prod-run 2155556666):
- model: mistral-7b-v2 (GQA): seq=512, batch=4
- num_attention_heads=48, num_key_value_heads=16
- head_dim=64, kv_head_dim=192
- chosen_kernel: generic_matmul (latency 2.3ms/token) fallback due to headstride != warp-optimal
- kernel_candidates: [warp_opt, frag_safe, generic_matmul]
- KV pages: avg page occupancy 42%, fragmentation=0.31, evict_rate spike @t0+3h
- batching: dynamic batching window=8ms -> observed small batch sizes (~2) during bursts
```
anya: that head/head-kv mismatch smells like MQA vs GQA config mix. When kv heads < attn heads we pad or reshape kv which may change strides. If kernel chooser only looks at attn head_dim it will misclassify.
alex: proposed quick fix: add heuristic that checks kv stride and prefers warp_opt when kv_head_dim % 32 == 0 and num_key_value_heads * kv_head_dim equals expected kv buffer stride. fallback flag in runtime: `force_kernel=warp_opt_if_kv_aligned`.
jiro: small repro I ran locally: switching `force_kernel` cut p99 by ~18% for the repro. repro config attached.
```
# repro command
./run_bench --model mistral-7b-v2 --batch 4 --seq 512 --num_kv_heads 16 --kv_dim 192 --force_kernel warp_opt
# perf delta
# baseline p99: 14.2ms -> with force_kernel p99: 11.6ms
```
maya: nice. but we should also address paged KV fragmentation — pages being underfilled leads to extra copy/merge overhead on eviction. observed on mixed seq workloads.
anya: thought: implement a compacting pass that coalesces small pages before eviction when fragmentation > 0.25 and traffic is write-heavy. cheap heuristic: if avg occupancy < 0.5 and free_pages > threshold then coalesce.
alex: sounds good. also think about batching heuristic: the dynamic window of 8ms is too small for bursts; increasing to 12-15ms improved batching and amortized kernel launch overhead in my test. tradeoff: ±3-5ms tail latency for amortized token throughput.
jiro: note: RoPE scaling differences between models (llama vs mixtral vs qwen) change numeric ranges, which influenced branch prediction inside fused kernel in one vendor kernel — we saw a regression where RoPE-scaling reduced fused attention throughput because of extra scaling ops moved into hot loop. might need kernel variants that hoist RoPE scaling out when possible.
maya: agree. for rollout plan: 1) add kv-alignment check to kernel chooser (hotfix flag), 2) bump dynamic batch window to 12ms behind a feature gate, 3) add periodic page-coalesce heuristic in KV manager, 4) run canary on dedicated pool for 24h.
perf-bot: deploy plan created: `canary/mistral7b/kernel-kv-fixes` -> allocated 6 nodes in eu-west1-dedicated. CI perf tests scheduled.
alex: i'll own the kernel-chooser change, will open PR with tests to cover kv-aligned and mismatched-heads cases.
jiro: i'll prototype page-coalesce and run a microbenchmark for mixed-sequence workloads (short+long).
anya: I'll update the rollout doc with regression gates (p95/p99/p50 and tokens/s cost). also add a prompt set for QoR checks (sampling for hallucination unchanged).
maya: thank you — if we can get the hotfix in tonight we can avoid further customer noise. :thumbsup:
alex: PR incoming in ~2h. tagging @maya for validation when landed.
